newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares lower as all eyes turn to Telekom.
newsitem.headline: German shares lower as all eyes turn to Telekom.

text.p: Germany's DAX index of leading shares finished lower on Monday as attention was overwhelmingly fixed on market debutant Deutsche Telekom AG, which was able in contrast to post a strong gain in bourse trade.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares, which the telecom giant will join on Tuesday, closed 31.96 points, or 1.14 percent, lower at 2,763.84 amid volumes described by traders as weak.

The IBIS DAX, measuring all-day computer trade in the DAX index, was down 31.70 points at 2,768.90 by 1715 GMT, somewhat higher than the bourse close, but held down by a lower start on Wall Street and a weaker dollar, bad for German exporters.
Deutsche Telekom opened bourse trade at 33.20 marks, well above its issue price of 28.50 marks, before going on to add a further 70 pfennigs to 33.90 marks at the bourse close.
Trading volume in the share was huge, with some 37.7 million shares changing hands during floor trade and almost 30 million in computerised IBIS dealings.
"There's only one subject today and that's Telekom. Don't go looking for much action elsewhere in the market," said one Frankfurt trader.
Later in the day, in specially-extended computer trade Telekom shares fell below their opening price and stood at 32.58 marks by the close, with dealers saying some players were taking profit.
Computer trading hours have been temporarily extended by two hours to accomodate the anticipated large volumes of Telekom dealings.
Telekom shares trading for the first time on Wall Street opened strongly above the issue price of $18.89 in heavy volumes hitting a high of $22-1/8. The stock is due to be traded in Tokyo on Tuesday.

Dealers said the main impact on the stock during the day had been buying by institutions seeking to top up small allocations in the issue, which was heavily-oversubscribed and saw an unparalleled amount of interest by small investors.

"There is still a good chance that it can improve on this (current) level. There are a couple of institutions out there that didn't get much of an allocation but still haven't gone into the market yet," said one trader.
Dealers said they were overly concerned that the price of Telekom shares would fall much further, with many seeing support at around 31 marks.

Activity elsewhere in the market was limited, but shares in retailer Karstadt were weaker, falling over three percent or 17.75 marks to 554.45 marks, after it announced it expect 1996 earnings to be below those 1995.
